findings.title: Agent repeats acknowledgment without progressing after barge-ins
findings.evidence_quote: no problem. I'll help you with a Thursday afternoon appoint.
findings.what_happened: After being interrupted twice, the agent produced two more short acknowledgment fragments (turns 004, 006) that restated the same 'I'll help with Thursday afternoon' idea instead of moving directly to the next required step, before finally asking for the name in turn 007.
findings.why_it_matters: Repeated re-acknowledgment without advancing the task wastes the caller's time and can feel like the agent is stuck in a loop, which is frustrating for a caller who has already repeated their request twice.
findings.expected_behaviour: After confirming it understood the Thursday afternoon request once, the agent should have moved straight to the next necessary step (e.g., asking for the name) rather than re-stating the same acknowledgment across multiple turns.

findings.title: Agent invents a date of birth the caller never provided
findings.evidence_quote: Your patient profile is set up. And your date of birth is 07/04/2000 for demo purposes. How can I help you today?
findings.what_happened: The agent stated a specific date of birth (07/04/2000) as though it were the caller's real recorded information, but the caller had never supplied a date of birth at any point in the conversation.
findings.why_it_matters: In a medical context, presenting fabricated identity data as fact risks corrupting patient records, causing identity mismatches, or misleading the patient about what information is on file, which can have downstream clinical and administrative consequences.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should have asked the caller for their date of birth rather than asserting an invented value, or clearly flagged that the value was a placeholder before treating it as confirmed patient data.

findings.title: Agent mid-sentence restart while stating existing appointment
findings.evidence_quote: You already have an office visit booked for Friday, September yeah. The office visit's already scheduled for Friday, September 4 at 03:30PM.
findings.what_happened: The agent began a sentence, cut itself off mid-word, and restarted the same sentence again without any interruption from the caller.
findings.why_it_matters: Even without caller interruption, self-restarting sentences suggests unstable turn/state tracking and can confuse the caller about what information is being conveyed, especially for appointment details.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should deliver the appointment detail in a single coherent sentence without restarting mid-way.
